headline: 20 Questions Deduction Game for ESL Question Formation Practice
outcomes: Students practise forming grammatically correct yes/no questions in a natural, game-driven context
Develop logical deduction and elimination strategies using English question structures
Build confidence asking questions spontaneously rather than from a scripted list
Reinforce topic vocabulary — the secret concept is always drawn from the lesson theme
howItWorks: One student picks a secret concept — a word, place, person, or object related to the class topic
The rest of the class takes turns submitting yes/no questions on their devices to narrow down possibilities
The secret holder answers each question; the class tracks answers and eliminates possibilities
The round ends when someone correctly identifies the secret — or when 20 questions are exhausted
teacherUseCases: Question formation practice where students must produce interrogative structures to progress
Vocabulary review — the secret concept forces students to think around the word rather than state it
Speaking fluency warm-up that feels like a game rather than a drill

faq.q: How does question quality affect scores?
faq.a: Points are awarded for grammatically correct questions. Poorly formed questions are flagged and the student can revise before submitting — making every question a mini grammar check.
Either a student chooses something from the topic, or the teacher enters a concept at the start. The AI can also generate a suitable secret concept based on the session topic.

faq.q: Can questions beyond yes/no be asked?
faq.a: The classic format uses yes/no questions only. Some teachers run it in 'expanded' mode where follow-up clarification questions are allowed — this can be managed by the teacher in the session settings.

faq.q: How do students submit their questions during play?
faq.a: Students type questions on their phone or tablet through a mobile browser. The session link is all they need — no app download or student account required.

faq.q: What level is this best suited to?
faq.a: 20 Questions works well from A2 upward. Lower levels benefit from the constraint of yes/no questions which are grammatically simpler. Higher levels can explore more creative, abstract questioning strategies.

faq.q: Is 20 Questions free to run in class?
faq.a: Yes, 20 Questions is free. Teachers start the session and students join through a browser link — no account setup required on either side.
